article.title: Local 256 Secures New Contract, Maintains Union Shop
article.content: Local 256 (MIT-GSU) ratified a new three-year contract with MIT on November 16. They successfully negotiated raises that keep up with inflation — the members will receive a wage increase of 3.5 percent in 2026 (with retroactive pay), 3.25 percent in 2027, and 3.25 percent in 2028. The members gained vacation flexibility, kept their healthcare benefits, and negotiated increased protections for international workers. The local also retained their union shop by organizing an effective strike threat that forced MIT to back down from their demand for an open shop. Local 256 Vice President of Membership Suveena Sreenilayam said, “We are incredibly excited to have won a fair second contract when it was the last thing MIT wanted to do. We know that building a credible strike threat is the only reason MIT was motivated to settle on all of our strike issues. “MIT came into these contract negotiations trying to gut our union by proposing an open shop. On Tuesday, we not only won back our union shop, we organized for protections that meet the moment, like an immigration support fund for international workers. This is thanks to every member and the tens of thousands of conversations we had over the past year to build our union power.” Stay tuned for more details about the contract and the organizational campaign that won it in the coming weeks.
